full_judgment:
2. The respondent No.1 Md Nurul Islam and others filed Title Suit No. 61 of 1982 in the court of Subordinate Judge, Satkhira against the defendant Md Aminul Islam and others for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for permanent injunction in respect of the suit lands described in the schedule to the plaint. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that the suit land together with other lands originally belonged to one Jonab Ali Sarder, who gave a settlement of the suit land measuring 27.38 acres in favour of his son-in-law Abdul Hamid in the middle of Baishakh, 1355 BS at a salami of Taka 3000.00 and yearly rent of Taka 135.00 12 annas and 6 pies. After this settlement, Abdul Hamid took over possession of the suit land and possessed the same. Abdul Hamid paid rent to the landlord, Janab Ali Sarder, but in course of time there was a default in payment of rent and that landlord Janab Ali instituted a Rent Suit No. 826 of 1956 in the 3rd Court of Munsif at Satkhira against Abdul Hamid for arrear of rent and got the decree. During SA operation the suit land was recorded in the SA Khatian in the name of Abdul Hamid within the knowledge of defendant Nos. 1-5. Abdul Hamid possessed the suit land and during his life time and then died in 1971 during liberation war of Bangladesh leaving behind his wife Jahura Khatun and 2 sons Baki Billah and Moniruzzaman. These heirs of Abdul Hamid possessed the suit land and paid rent to the government. They also submitted a statement of property including the suit land under President''s Order No. 98 of 1972. They thereafter transferred 0.60 decimals of land out of plot No. 294 to defendant No. 15 by a registered kabala. Thereafter Jahura, Baki, Moniruzzaman jointly transferred the suit land measuring 26.77 acres to the plaintiffs by 5 registered kabalas dated 9-3-1982 and 10-3-1982 and made over possession of the same to the plaintiffs. Since purchase, the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land as of their own right and paying rent to the Government. The defendants have no right, title or possession in the suit land but that the defendants threatened the plaintiffs on 28th Jaistha, 1389 BS corresponding to 23-6-82 to remove earth from the suit land thereby disturbing the plaintiffs' peaceful possession therein. Hence, the plaintiffs have filed the suit for declaration as aforesaid. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1-5 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying the material allegations and statements made in the plaint. The defendants' case, in short, is that the suit land appertaining to CS Khatian No. 6 originally belonged to Jonab Ali Sarder. This Jonab Ali Sarder subsequently made a settlement of 27.38. acres of land to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in the first part of Baishakh, 1358 BS at a rental of Taka 131 and 3 annas, At the time of this settlement, these two defendants were minors and that their maternal grand-fathers, Jonab Ali Moral and Mohor Ali Sardar respectively did everything in taking settlement and in paying the rent and salami to the landlord Jonab Ali Sarder. Their maternal grand-fathers paid a salami of Taka 4000.00 on behalf of the defendants to Jonab Ali Sarder and that Jonab Ali Sarder granted dakhila to the defendants. Since settlement, the defendants'' maternal grandfathers used to possess the suit land and look after the same during their lifetime on behalf of the defendants. After the death of their grand-fathers, the defendants 1 and 2 themselves have been possessing the suit land. The PRR Khatian was prepared in the name of defendants in respect of the suit land but subsequently the name of Abdul Hamid was recorded wrongly in the SA Khatian. The defendants filed an objection case against this wrong record under section 19(1) of EBSAT Act and that an order was passed in favour of defendants for correction of wrong SA Khatian but that this order was not complied with. Subsequently, the defendants by filing an application in the office of the ADC got their names recorded in a mutation Khatian and paid rent to the government. The defendants thus have been owning and possessing the suit land. The plaintiffs or Abdul Hamid or his heirs have no right, title or possession in the suit land. The defendants'' uncle or mother never filed any suit in the Sub-Judge Court at Khulna in respect of the suit land as stated by the plaintiff in the plaint. All these are fictitious papers without basis. The plaintiff's kabalas are some paper transactions without consideration and it did not create any title to the suit land in favour of the plaintiff. As such, the plaintiff''s suit is liable to be dismissed.
